Subject: Borealis request: exec sign-off for SLO adjustment and credit cap (BOR-2391)

Team — forwarding a condensed ask from Borealis (Ethan Clarke) and attaching our proposed redline + MAP. High level: they're asking for a non-standard uptime target (drop from our standard 99.95% to 99.5%) for the initial 12-month term because their workload has extreme cold-start spikes and they're routing via a 3rd-party gateway. They are also requesting a 15% first-year discount and removal of our standard rolling remedies (they want a capped, one-time credit).

Why this matters: Borealis is a high-profile utility customer and fast pilot conversion is strategic, but we need to avoid open-ended credit exposure and precedent-setting language. Proposed commercial response (attached PDF):
- Temporary SLO: 99.5% uptime for first 6 months, revert to 99.95% thereafter unless both parties agree in writing.
- Service credit: capped at $10,000 over the first 12 months (all incidents combined).
- Operational make-up plan: 2 on-site / hands-on sessions from our SREs in month 1 to optimize routing and caching (no additional charge).
- Discount: can approve up to 10% first-year ARR credit; 15% requires exec approval.

Ask: Need exec sign-off on (a) allowing the temporary SLO, (b) the $10k credit cap, and (c) discount ceiling. Also asking Legal to confirm that the attached redline contains proper rollback language and no binding indefinite remedies.

Attachments: BOR-2391_SLA_proposed_redline.pdf, BOR-2391_MAP.xlsx

Thanks Monica — quick clarifications before I commit:
1) Is the $10k cap against monthly invoices or an aggregate credit across the 12 months?
2) What metrics/alerting will Borealis accept to trigger the credit (we should avoid vague language).
3) If we agree to the temporary SLO, who owns the remediation timeline and acceptance criteria for the make-up sessions?

If the cap is aggregate and the make-up plan requires our ops time (but we own scope), I am comfortable with up to a 10% discount. 15% needs an explicit ROI case and signoff from Finance.

Can you paste the customer's suggested language inline so Legal can do a fast redline?

—Aditya

Subject: Re: Borealis request: exec sign-off for SLO adjustment and credit cap (BOR-2391)

Aditya — answers inline and pasted the customer's proposed paragraph below (they sent it earlier today).

1) $10k = aggregate cap over first 12 months (all incidents combined).
2) Customer suggested triggers: any incident that causes response-time degradation >200ms P50 over a 1-hour window for >3 consecutive minutes. We should tighten to P95 or specify token-latency for generation endpoints.
3) Redwood would own the remediation deliverables; customer wants acceptance testing in their staging environment before cutover. Proposed operational scope in the MAP (attached): two SRE workshops in month 1, a configuration checkpoint at week 6, and a final acceptance window.

Customer suggested paragraph (verbatim):
"Redwood agrees to a Temporary Service Level of 99.5% uptime for the Initial Term. In the event of Service Unavailability or Degradation as defined in this Agreement, Customer may be eligible for Service Credits as set forth herein."

My recommended replacement (to avoid open-ended remedies):
"Redwood and Customer agree to a Temporary Service Level of 99.5% uptime for the Initial Term (first 6 months). Service Credits, if any, will be calculated per incident and are subject to an aggregate cap of $10,000 across the Initial Term. Service Credits will be triggered only by incidents meeting the P95 token-latency threshold defined in Appendix A. Redwood will provide operational assistance described in the Mutual Action Plan and will retain final authority over remediation acceptance criteria. Unless extended in writing by both parties, the Temporary Service Level will revert to Redwood's Standard Service Level (99.95%) at the end of the Initial Term."

I also pushed back on the 15% discount and asked for a pipeline commitment to justify anything above 10%. Ethan confirmed they can consider a 9–12 month ramp and introduced their CPO on the thread (copied).

Attachments: BOR-2391_MAP.xlsx (scope & schedule)

Monica Patel
Enterprise Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Borealis request: exec sign-off for SLO adjustment and credit cap (BOR-2391)

Monica / Aditya — after reviewing the summary and attachments I am comfortable approving a conditional exception with the following firm guardrails (signoff below):
- Temporary SLO may be set to 99.5% for the Initial Term, limited to 6 months; any extension requires a documented business case and Finance sign-off.
- Aggregate service credit cap: $10,000. Credits must be charged against invoices and cannot exceed the cap.
- Discount: approve up to 10% first-year ARR credit; anything >10% must be escalated with explicit revenue/ARR justification (I will not approve 15% without a clear compensation plan).
- Operational make-up plan is acceptable, subject to a scope statement in the MAP and a weekly milestone cadence (deliverables to be logged in the MAP spreadsheet).
- Legal: confirm the redline contains a clear rollback clause and that acceptance criteria reference a defined Appendix A (latency thresholds).
- Executive condition: require a joint health-check signoff at month 3.

If these conditions are met, I sign off for Deal Desk to proceed with the customer and finalize the contract with the attached redline language (subject to Legal tidy-up).

Grace O'Connor
VP Finance, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
